question: According to the Delaware CDL manual, what can happen to a commercial vehicle that is overloaded?
choice_a: Steering, braking, and speed control can all be affected, and stopping distance increases
choice_b: The vehicle automatically shifts into a lower gear to compensate
choice_c: Only fuel economy is reduced, with no effect on handling
choice_d: The parking brake becomes more effective at holding the vehicle
explanation: The manual states overloading can have bad effects on steering, braking, and speed control; overloaded trucks go slowly on upgrades but may gain too much speed on downgrades, stopping distance increases, and brakes can fail when forced to work too hard.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-2

question: When is a high center of gravity from top-heavy cargo most dangerous?
choice_a: In curves or when you have to swerve to avoid a hazard
choice_b: Only when the vehicle is parked on an incline
choice_d: Only at highway speeds on straight roads
explanation: The manual explains a high center of gravity means you are more likely to tip over, and this is most dangerous in curves or if you have to swerve to avoid a hazard.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-2

question: How should cargo be distributed to keep the vehicle's center of gravity as low as possible?
choice_a: Put the heaviest parts of the cargo under the lightest parts
choice_b: Put the heaviest parts of the cargo on top of the lightest parts
choice_c: Distribute all cargo weight toward the rear axles only
choice_d: It does not matter, as long as the total weight is legal
explanation: The manual states it is very important to distribute the cargo so it is as low as possible, and to put the heaviest parts of the cargo under the lightest parts.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-2

question: What can result from too much weight on the steering axle?
choice_a: Hard steering, which can damage the steering axle and tires
explanation: The manual states poor weight balance can make vehicle handling unsafe, and too much weight on the steering axle can cause hard steering and can damage the steering axle and tires.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-2

question: What can cause the steering axle to become too light to steer safely?
choice_a: Shifting weight too far to the rear, resulting in an under-loaded front axle
choice_b: Shifting all weight to the front of the trailer
choice_c: Using tie-downs that are too strong for the cargo
choice_d: Loading cargo evenly across all axles
explanation: The manual explains that under-loaded front axles, caused by shifting weight too far to the rear, can make the steering axle weight too light to steer safely.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-2

question: What problem can occur if there is too little weight on the driving axles?
choice_a: Poor traction, and the drive wheels may spin easily, especially in bad weather
choice_b: The vehicle will be unable to brake at all
choice_d: The parking brake will fail to release
explanation: The manual states too little weight on the driving axles can cause poor traction, the drive wheels may spin easily, and during bad weather the truck may not be able to keep going.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-2

question: What is the difference between blocking and bracing when securing cargo?
choice_a: Blocking fits snugly against cargo to keep it from sliding, while bracing goes from the upper part of the cargo to the floor and/or walls
choice_b: Blocking and bracing are two names for the exact same technique
choice_c: Bracing is only used on flatbed trailers, while blocking is only used in closed vans
choice_d: Blocking is used only for hanging meat loads
explanation: The manual states blocking is shaped to fit snugly against cargo and is secured to the cargo deck to prevent movement, while bracing goes from the upper part of the cargo to the floor and/or walls of the cargo compartment.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-2

question: According to the manual, what is the minimum number of tie-downs required for any piece of cargo, no matter how small?
choice_d: No tie-downs are required if the cargo is small
explanation: The manual states cargo should have at least one tie-down for each ten feet of cargo, and no matter how small the cargo, it should have at least two tie-downs.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-3

question: Under federal regulations described in the manual, the aggregate working load limit of a cargo securement system must be at least how much of the weight of the article or group of articles it secures?
explanation: The manual states federal regulations require the aggregate working load limit of any securement system used to secure an article or group of articles against movement must be at least one-half times the weight of the article or group of articles.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-2

question: Which of the following are examples of proper tie-down equipment mentioned in the manual?
choice_a: Ropes, straps, chains, and tensioning devices such as winches and ratchets
choice_b: Duct tape and bungee cords only
choice_c: Only metal chains, with no other materials allowed
explanation: The manual states proper tie-down equipment must be used, including ropes, straps, chains, and tensioning devices (winches, ratchets, clinching components), attached correctly with hooks, bolts, rails, or rings.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-2

question: What is the purpose of a front-end header board ("headache rack")?
choice_a: To protect the driver from cargo in case of a crash or emergency stop
choice_b: To increase the vehicle's fuel efficiency
choice_c: To provide extra storage space for tools
choice_d: To display the vehicle's DOT number
explanation: The manual states front-end header boards protect the driver from cargo in case of a crash or emergency stop, and the front-end structure should block the forward movement of any cargo carried.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-3

question: What are the two basic reasons for covering cargo, according to the manual?
choice_a: To protect people from spilled cargo and to protect the cargo from weather
choice_b: To reduce vehicle weight and improve fuel economy
choice_c: To hide the cargo from view and to reduce wind noise
choice_d: To keep the cargo warm and to prevent theft
explanation: The manual lists two basic reasons for covering cargo: to protect people from spilled cargo, and to protect the cargo from weather.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-3

question: Since a driver cannot inspect a sealed load's contents, what should the driver check instead?
choice_a: That the vehicle does not exceed gross weight and axle weight limits
choice_b: The internal temperature of the container only
choice_c: Nothing, since sealed loads require no inspection at all
choice_d: The identity of the shipper listed on the seal
explanation: The manual states you cannot inspect sealed loads, but you should check that you don't exceed gross weight and axle weight limits.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-3

question: When are containerized loads generally used, according to the manual?
choice_a: When freight is carried part way by rail or ship, with truck delivery at the beginning and/or end of the journey
choice_c: Only for loads that do not require any securement
choice_d: Only within a single city's local delivery routes
explanation: The manual states containerized loads generally are used when freight is carried part way by rail or ship, with delivery by truck occurring at the beginning and/or end of the journey; some containers have their own tie-down devices, while others must be loaded onto flatbed trailers and secured like any other cargo.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-3

question: Why do dry bulk tanks require special care while driving?
choice_a: They have a high center of gravity and the load can shift
choice_b: They are exempt from all weight limits
choice_c: They cannot be driven on highways
choice_d: They never need to be inspected
explanation: The manual states dry bulk tanks require special care because they have a high center of gravity and the load can shift, so drivers should be extremely cautious going around curves and making sharp turns.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-3

question: Why is hanging meat (suspended beef, pork, or lamb) in a refrigerated truck considered a particularly unstable load?
choice_a: It has a high center of gravity, requiring particular caution on sharp curves such as off ramps and on ramps
choice_b: It is heavier than any other type of cargo allowed on a CDL vehicle
choice_c: It requires no tie-downs at all
choice_d: It cannot be transported in a refrigerated truck
explanation: The manual states hanging meat can be a very unstable load with a high center of gravity, and particular caution is needed on sharp curves such as off ramps and on ramps, so drivers should go slowly.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-3

question: What technique does the manual recommend to keep livestock bunched together when a trailer has less than a full load?
choice_b: Increase vehicle speed to reduce shifting
choice_d: Fill the empty space with dry bulk cargo
explanation: The manual states that with less than a full load, false bulkheads should be used to keep livestock bunched together, since livestock can lean on curves, shifting the center of gravity and making rollover more likely.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-3

question: What do over-length, over-width, and/or overweight loads require, according to the manual?
choice_a: Special transit permits, and driving is usually limited to certain times
choice_b: No special documentation, only a verbal notification to dispatch
choice_c: A reduction in tire pressure before departure
choice_d: Removal of all warning lights and signs to avoid distracting other drivers
explanation: The manual states over-length, over-width, and/or overweight loads require special transit permits, driving is usually limited to certain times, and special equipment such as wide load signs, flashing lights, and flags may be necessary, sometimes with a police escort or pilot vehicles.
source_note: Delaware CDL Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, Version 4.0, Release Date: February 2025, AAMVA Modernized Testing System), Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 3 - Transporting Cargo Safely, p. 3-3
